facts.statement: The genus was described by Xiao-Chun Wu and colleagues in 2001, with the type species designated as Rugosuchus nonganensis.
facts.quote: It was described by Xiao-Chun Wu and colleagues in 2001, with R. nonganensis as the type species.

facts.statement: When first described, Rugosuchus was the most complete crocodyliform known from northeastern China and the second such fossil found in that region.
facts.quote: At the time of its description, it was the most complete crocodyliform from northeastern China, and only the second known.

facts.statement: At the time of its description, the age of the formation where Rugosuchus was found was thought to be the latest Early Cretaceous based on associated ostracode, bivalve, and fish fossils.
facts.quote: The age of the Nenjiang Formation has been debated, but as of the description of Rugosuchus was thought to be latest Early Cretaceous, based on ostracode, bivalve, and fish fossils.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies have generally reclassified the age of the Rugosuchus formation as the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: However, most of later studies consider it as late Cretaceous instead.

facts.statement: The primary skull specimen, IGV 33, is believed to belong to an adult individual based on bone fusion.
facts.quote: Skull IGV 33 is thought to have come from an adult, based on the fusion of bones.

facts.statement: The skull is somewhat elongate, measuring approximately 28 centimeters (11 inches) in length and 13 centimeters (5 inches) at its widest point.
facts.quote: It is somewhat elongate, being about 28 centimeters (11 in) long but only an estimated 13 centimeters (5 in) at its widest.

facts.statement: The premaxillae at the snout tip held five teeth each, while the maxillae held 16 or 17 teeth with wide spacing.
facts.quote: The premaxillae at the tip of the snout had five teeth each, and the maxillae 16 or 17, with wide spacing

facts.statement: Wu et al. determined Rugosuchus was not an eusuchian due to palatal bone structure, but suggested it was more closely related to eusuchians than genera like Goniopholis because it possessed more than two rows of bony armor.
facts.quote: Wu et al. noted that their new genus was not an eusuchian because of the form of the palatal bones, but it was probably more closely related to the eusuchians than other extinct crocodyliforms like Goniopholis by having more than two rows of bony armor running its length, and by the form of the armor.

facts.statement: A 2008 phylogenetic analysis by Turner and Buckley placed Rugosuchus in a clade with Eusuchia alongside the "Glen Rose Form," suggesting it is more derived than Bernissartia.
facts.quote: However, a more recent phylogenetic analysis by Turner and Buckley (2008) places it with the "Glen Rose Form" in a clade with Eusuchia, more derived than Bernissartia.

facts.statement: The parent group of Rugosuchus is classified as Paralligatoridae.
Rugosuchus belongs to the family Paralligatoridae.
The time range for Rugosuchus is the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
